title: Bicarbonate–anion-gap coupling adds no demonstrated cross-cycle FEV1 prediction beyond individual chemistry measures
abstract: A fixed bicarbonate-by-anion-gap interaction did not improve concurrent FEV1 prediction beyond flexible additive anthropometry, smoking and routine chemistry. We fitted 3,729 NHANES 2007–2008 adults and evaluated frozen models in 4,096 separately recruited 2009–2010 adults. Target RMSE changed from 445.286 to 445.328 mL: baseline-minus-augmented gain −0.042 mL (target stratified-PSU bootstrap 95% interval −0.115 to +0.029; source/target refit interval −0.624 to +0.117). Against a weaker anthropometry-only comparator, the same interaction yielded a small +0.607 mL gain, illustrating baseline dependence; additive individual chemistry instead gained +4.989 mL. These are same-programme, cross-sectional, selected-sample prediction results, not acid-base diagnoses, causation or clinical benefit. Self-checks and fresh offline reruns are supplied; independent-programme validation remains missing.
